record.original_question: Let X and Y be positive operators, let p≥2, and define the weighted power mean M_t=(tX^p+(1-t)Y^p)^(1/p) for 0≤t≤1. Is the squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance from Y to M_t, namely Tr(Y-M_t)^2, always a monotonically increasing function of t on [0,1]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be positive (semidefinite) operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and let $p \geq 2$ be a real number. For $0 \leq t \leq 1$, define the weighted power mean
$$M_t \;=\; \bigl(t X^{p} + (1-t) Y^{p}\bigr)^{1/p}.$$
Consider the function
$$\varphi(t) \;=\; \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(Y - M_t\bigr)^{2} \;=\; \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(Y - (t X^{p} + (1-t) Y^{p})^{1/p}\bigr)^{2}, \qquad t \in [0,1],$$
which measures the squared Hilbert–Schmidt distance from $Y$ to $M_t$. Prove or disprove: for every choice of positive operators $X, Y$ and every $p \geq 2$, the function $\varphi$ is monotonically increasing on $[0,1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published proof or disproof of this specific monotonicity conjecture for the squared Hilbert–Schmidt distance from $Y$ to the weighted $p$-power mean for $p\geq 2$. Related Bhatia-type conjectures (e.g., Bhatia–Li monotonicity in $p$, and Bhatia–Lim–Yamazaki) have been resolved, but none of the located references address this precise statement, so its current status appears unknown from accessible sources.

status_evidence.title: A positive answer to Bhatia–Li conjecture on the monotonicity for a new mean in its parameter
status_evidence.snippet: Bhatia and Li conjectured that the Bhatia-Li mean Bp(x,y) is an increasing function of the parameter p; a positive answer was given.
status_evidence.claim: Related Bhatia-type monotonicity conjectures have been resolved, but for a different mean/parameter, not for the present trace-distance statement.

status_evidence.title: On a conjecture of Bhatia, Lim and Yamazaki
status_evidence.snippet: A conjecture of Bhatia, Lim and Yamazaki on matrix power means has been proved.
status_evidence.claim: A different Bhatia-type conjecture on power means has been settled; this does not address the specific Hilbert–Schmidt monotonicity question.
